rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: curriculum/lectures/ is shared-library by directory convention (curriculum/CLAUDE.md § Directory); maintainer fence at current L67. Grep of the raw body (L1-66) confirms four M[0-9] hits, unchanged since the 2026-08-03 audit and the prior two story instances: L3 'the M5/M6 loop', L17 'Chat-shaped in the exact way M5 teaches you to notice', L47 'I ran the M6 exercise on the M6 generation', L55 'diagnose gaps in the M5 packaged session'. Harm-check (dispatch preamble, mandatory before any REVISE): the rule exists to protect re-placeability — a lecture bridging to a named prior/future module breaks if the file is later moved to a different sequence position, or asks an out-of-context reader to hold a reference they haven't earned. Neither harm is present: (1) portability — the maintainer block (current L91) states this file is regenerated per cohort from that cohort's own session and is permanently, by design, M6's own opener; it will never be relocated to a different module slot, unlike a genuinely shared-library lecture, so there is no future move for a bare 'M5' to break. (2) comprehension — the cached persona trace (fresh, re-verified this pass) rates L17's M5 reference 'low friction — resolves within the numbers section' and explicitly notes the in-room, warm-off-M5 reader experiences it as 'recognition, not confusion.' With both harms absent, filing a REVISE here would ask the maintainer to fix a shape-match that costs nothing to leave and something (the file's own clarity) to change. Downgraded from REVISE to PASS this pass — the two prior story instances flagged this at REVISE/non-blocking without running the harm-check the current dispatch preamble requires before filing one; re-reading against that requirement changes the verdict, not just the framing.
